newsitem.title: UK: Sony soars in London on bullish statement.
newsitem.headline: Sony soars in London on bullish statement.

text.p: Shares in Sony Corp were up sharply in London after the company said in Tokyo on Wednesday that profits would climb to a record high this business year, powered by strong sales of electronic goods and a weak yen.
"The trading statement was terrific. The market had been looking to upgrade earnings forecasts but this has taken a few people by surprise," one market maker said.
Sony was trading at 8,415 yen by 1315 GMT after closing in Tokyo at 8,220 yen.
The company's third-quarter results and trading statment were released after the Tokyo share market closed on Wednesday.
For the October-December quarter, Sony reported group net profit of 75.38 billion yen($612 million), up 103 percent.
The strong performance led Sony to sharply revise upward group sales and profit for the year to end-March 1997.
"Almost all our our electronic products -- especially videogame players, minidiscs and camcorders-- are doing well...in all markets," Sony's finance director Sumio Sano told a news conference.
Sony now expects group net profit of 132 billion yen ($1.07 billion), nearly 2.5 times the net profit in the 1995/96 business year.
Analysts had expected Sony to report full-year profits of between 122 billion yen ($991 million) to 130 billion yen ($1.05 billion).
